Description: State park renowned for Onondaga Cave, a National Natural Landmark with spectacular cave formations. The river landing is at the Hwy H bridge on the northeast corner. A concrete boat ramp sits upstream of the bridge on the west side, and a canoe launch is downstream in the picnic grounds. 1,317 acres with campground, trails, and cave tours.

Road access: From I-44 exit 214 (Leasburg), take Hwy H south approximately 7 miles through Leasburg. Paved road throughout. The state river landing is on the northeast corner of the Hwy H bridge. Address: 7556 Hwy H, Leasburg, MO 65535.

Parking: Paved parking near visitor center and day-use areas. Two overflow lots near the campsite area. Short walk to canoe launch from day-use parking. Trailer access at the boat ramp parking area.

Facilities: Concrete boat ramp upstream of bridge (west side) and separate canoe launch downstream in picnic grounds. 19 basic + 45 premium (electric/water) + 3 accessible campsites. Shower houses with hot water near campsites (seasonal April–October). Laundry facility. RV dump station. Fire rings, picnic tables, lantern hangers. Playground, amphitheater. Vault toilets at day-use areas. 6 miles of trails. Cave tours: Onondaga Cave ($15 adults, $9 ages 6–12) and Cathedral Cave ($20 adults, $12 ages 6–12). Visitor center with gift shop.

Fees: No entrance or launch fee. Camping fees vary by site type. Cave tour fees separate.

Meramec State Park
2356fe98-53d5-4e24-98d2-6f2514bb5636
meramec/meramec-state-park

Description: Missouri's most-visited state park on the Meramec River. 6,896 acres with over 40 caves, 13 miles of hiking trails, and a scenic stretch of river. The upper boat ramp near Campground 3 and the park store is the primary launch for floaters. Concession operates canoe/kayak/raft rentals with shuttle service. Popular float: Meramec SP to Onondaga Cave SP (approximately 20 miles, full day).

Road access: From I-44 exit 226 (Sullivan), turn left off the exit, go 3 miles south on Hwy 185 to the park entrance. All paved roads. Address: 115 Meramec Park Drive, Sullivan, MO 63080.

Parking: Spacious paved parking lot near boat ramp accommodates vehicles and trailers. Four large parking lots at the campground. Ample room for oversized vehicles.

Facilities: Concrete motorboat launch and separate canoe/kayak launch near park store and Campground 3. Campground 3: 32 sites with electric hookups, picnic tables, fire rings (driveways 35–63 ft accommodate RVs). Shower house with hot water and laundry (seasonal April–October). RV dump station. Frost-free water spigot available Nov–April. Visitor center, gift shop, camp store, restaurant. Three picnic shelters (reservable, capacity ~75 each). Cave tours (Cathedral Cave, Fisher Cave). 13 miles of trails. Canoe/kayak/raft rentals and shuttle service through park concession.

Fees: No entrance or launch fee. Camping $12–$48/night depending on site type. Shelter reservations $35/day. Canoe/kayak/raft rental fees vary.

Description: Remote MDC access within the Meramec Conservation Area at approximately mile 92. Carry-in access only — no boat ramp. Road access: From I-44 near Sullivan, take Hwy 185 south approximately 5 miles past the Meramec Work Station. Turn left onto Rt. K, follow 1.4 miles, turn left onto Spanish Claim Road (gravel). Follow approximately 4.5 miles to the dead-end parking area. Road is entirely gravel and is not well-marked on maps. Remote location.

Parking: Gravel parking lot — has been upgraded from formerly muddy conditions. An old concrete silo marks the location. Boats must be carried approximately 100–200 yards to the river, making trailer access impractical.

Facilities: Carry-in access only. No boat ramp. Trail (100–200 yards) through woods to gravel bar and river — has been cleared and widened in recent years. No restrooms at this specific access point. The broader Meramec Conservation Area offers 10.5 miles of multi-use trails, paved ADA walking path, horseback riding, and 6 caves.

Description: Private campground and river access at the famous Meramec Caverns in Stanton at mile 94.3. The LaJolla Natural Park campground sits along the Meramec River with direct launch access. Canoe, kayak, and raft rentals with shuttle — 6-mile and 11-mile float options with shuttle upstream and float back to the caverns. Also home to Missouri's most visited show cave.

Road access: From I-44, take Exit 230 (Stanton). Follow signs to Meramec Caverns — approximately 3 miles south on Hwy W. Well-signed from the interstate. All paved roads. Address: 1135 Highway W, Stanton, MO 63079.

Parking: Large paved parking lot shared with cave visitors. Ample space for 50+ vehicles. Trailer-friendly.

Facilities: LaJolla Natural Park campground: ~40 electric-only sites, ~40 electric/water sites, primitive tent sites. Dump station at entrance (no sewer hookups at sites). Motel rooms also available. Shower houses with restrooms. Concession stand/restaurant, pavilions, playground, barbecue pits. Canoe/kayak/raft rentals via Cavern Canoe and Raft Rental (seasonal, April–September). Zip line, Jesse James Wax Museum, cave tours. One vehicle per campsite; extra vehicles must park in visitor lot.

Fees: Rental-only river access — personal watercraft (canoes, kayaks, tubes) NOT permitted to launch or take out on the property. Must rent from Cavern Canoe and Raft Rental. For BYO boats, use MDC Sand Ford Access (mile 95.4) next door instead. Campground open April 1 – October 31. Call (573) 468-3166 for reservations.

Description: MDC access on the Meramec at mile 66.2, near the Hwy E bridge and the Huzzah Conservation Area. Just upstream of where Huzzah Creek enters the Meramec at mile 66.3. The Huzzah and Courtois Creeks significantly boost the Meramec's flow from here downstream. Part of the 6,225-acre Huzzah Conservation Area.

Road access: From Steelville, take Hwy E northeast approximately 8 miles to the Meramec crossing area. From I-44 at Leasburg, take Hwy H south, then local roads west. Last stretch is gravel.

Parking: Gravel parking area at the low-water bridge area. Space for approximately 15 vehicles.

Facilities: Within Huzzah Conservation Area. Vault toilets at main parking area. Primitive camping allowed Sept 15 – May 15 (day use only remainder of year). No water, no trash service — pack in, pack out. Ozark Trail access nearby.

Fees: —

Ha Ha Tonka State Park
fe42a39c-7647-4b7d-91a4-f016d1214e36
niangua/ha-ha-tonka-state-park

Description: Free carry-in kayak access at the spring, the Lake of the Ozarks/Big Niangua River Trail terminus and 13.3 miles downstream of Whistle Bridge. The park provides stone kayak-launch steps and a launch rail, not a boat ramp; the first portion upstream is lake paddling. The castle ruins, spring and geology are the park's draw.

Road access: State Highway D south from Camdenton. Kayak launch: Tonka Spring Road, left from spring parking lot at Lakeside Picnic Shelter.

Parking: Multiple parking areas. Spring parking lot for kayak launch.

Facilities: Stone kayak-launch steps and launch rail; courtesy docks (24-foot limit); restrooms, picnic areas and trails. No boat ramp and no camping.

Fees: No launch fee.

Off-channel explanation: Park access is on the Lake of the Ozarks arm rather than the Niangua channel proper.

Agency / ownership: State Park / state_park

Description: MDC access at the Highway 72 bridge, the put-in for the 'Upper St. Francis' Class I-II whitewater run down to Millstream Gardens. The NWS/USGS Roselle gauge (07034000/ROZM7) that paddlers use for the runnable range is at this bridge. Gravel ramp serves the slow pool above the bridge for fishing when levels are low.

Road access: From Fredericktown take Highway 72 west 12 miles to the St. Francis River bridge and turn left immediately past the bridge (access is southwest of the bridge).

Parking: Gravel parking lot next to the ramp.

Facilities: Gravel/dirt boat ramp near the parking lot; 21.9-acre MDC access at the confluence area of the St. Francis River and Stouts Creek. No camping (prohibited). Cafe and store historically nearby on Hwy 72.

Millstream Gardens Conservation Area (Tiemann Shut-Ins put-in)
42aad76d-0c11-448e-bd2e-190a889c5050
st-francis/millstream-gardens-conservation-area

Description: MDC conservation area in Madison County that is the put-in for Missouri's only Class II-IV whitewater run, the 2.3-mile Tiemann Shut-Ins reach down to Silver Mines. Paddlers carry down a short slope to a gravel put-in on river-left just above the rapids. The Missouri Whitewater Championships run this reach each spring.

Road access: From Fredericktown take Highway 72 west 8 miles to the area entrance, then follow the area road south to the river parking lots; Route D reaches the area from the south side of the river.

Parking: Designated gravel/paved lots inside the conservation area near the put-in; vehicle use restricted to established parking areas.

Facilities: Carry-down gravel put-in on river-left above the Tiemann Shut-Ins (no constructed boat ramp); picnic areas, hiking trails and an accessible boardwalk to the shut-ins overlook within the 915.9-acre area.

Fees: —

Silver Mines Recreation Area (D-Bridge take-out)
1a0794ea-4470-4e7b-80b4-19414c1a9176
st-francis/silver-mines-recreation-area-hwy-d

Description: Mark Twain National Forest recreation area at the old Highway D bridge, the take-out for the Millstream Gardens/Tiemann Shut-Ins whitewater run and a put-in for the calmer float below. Slipways flank the old bridge (now a footbridge) with day-use areas on both banks and campgrounds on both sides of the river. Site of the historic Einstein silver mine and dam.

Road access: From Fredericktown go west on Highway 72 about 4.3 miles, turn left (south) on Highway D for 2.9 miles, then turn right at the bottom of the hill at the USFS camping sign into the recreation area.

Parking: Day-use parking lots by the old Highway D bridge (the standard whitewater take-out meeting spot) plus paved/gravel spurs in the campground loops.

Facilities: USFS campground with 70 individual sites (11 electric) in four loops plus a group site, ADA vault toilets, potable water, picnic tables; two day-use areas with river access at the old D bridge. Carry-in access, no constructed boat ramp. No showers or dump station.

Fees: $5 per vehicle per day day-use fee ($10/bus, $40 season pass); camping $15-$35 per night depending on site/electric.

Off-channel explanation: —

Agency / ownership: USFS / USFS

Official source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r09/marktwain/recreation/silver-mines-recreation-area

Sam A. Baker State Park boat launch (Campground 1)
5186d1c7-c1ef-437a-a202-725652949e85
st-francis/sam-a-baker-state-park-access

Description: The state park's river access is a concrete boat launch at Campground 1 on the St. Francis River, usually shallow enough that only canoes, kayaks and small boats can launch. The park store rents canoes, kayaks and rafts for floats of roughly 4-18 miles on the St. Francis (Big Creek is kayak-only in high water). Below the park the river noticeably slows toward Wappapello Lake.

Road access: From Highway 34 take Highway 143 north into the park (Patterson, Wayne County); the launch is at Campground 1 at the south end of the park on the St. Francis River.

Parking: Paved campground/day-use parking at Campground 1 near the launch.

Facilities: Concrete boat launch on the St. Francis River at Campground 1, open except during heavy flooding; no launch fee. Full-service state park: campgrounds with showers, cabins, dining lodge, and the Mudlick Mountain park store with canoe/kayak/raft rental (floats April-November).

Fees: No boat launch fee; camping/cabin fees apply for overnight stays.

st-francis/lake-creek

Description: COE recreation area on the right bank of the St. Francis River at the head of Wappapello Lake, the standard last take-out below Sam A. Baker before the lake. Boat ramp with courtesy dock in the day-use area plus a large full-hookup campground on the Old Greenville townsite. Big Lake Creek enters on river-right just upstream (the old float charts' 'Lake Creek, campground' point at mile 76.4).

Road access: From US 67 at Greenville use the Old Greenville exit; the day-use boat ramp is on the east side of Highway 67 on the west bank of the St. Francis River.

Parking: Paved day-use parking beside the ramp (OSM-mapped lot adjacent).

Facilities: US Army Corps of Engineers campground (106 full-hookup sites, showers, renovated 2019) with a day-use area: boat ramp with courtesy dock, 14 picnic sites, shelter, playground. Staffed April-November; built on the Old Greenville townsite.

Fees: A fee/day-use pass is required to use the boat ramp (Greenville Recreation Area Day Use Pass via Recreation.gov); amount not verified. Camping fees via Recreation.gov.

Validation, known constraints and remaining verification
  • Fresh live API check: 28 rivers × three request modes; all 84 succeeded. Identity/role/eligibility and selected location/display fields were compared, not byte equality of compact and full responses.
  • Seven additional requests checked the offline bundle and the POI/service responses for Current, Jacks Fork and Buffalo. The bundle contains all 25 active rivers and 325 approved accesses.
  • A fresh validate_river_data() query returned the two segment issues in F19. It also returned a Jacks Fork near Mountain View gauge threshold-order error, which is outside this access-data scope and should remain a separate condition-system finding.
  • The repository was read at f08f0f3b86acfd628b32baf1275f136c719069e8. No changes to its working tree were made. No build/test suite was run because this is an audit rather than an implementation; the evidence checks are live read-only comparisons and record identity/count assertions.
  • Current database and public response values take precedence over old migration intent. The existing September spring repair is present in source but its intended output is still absent in live data.
  • Coordinates, permissions, seasonal closures and exact launch approaches in the explicitly marked verification queue remain unconfirmed. The original pin coordinate is not automatically a road entrance; all 325 active approved access rows have null dedicated driving coordinates.

Recommended correction order

  1. Repair destination identity: Alley first, then Pulltite and Greer. Preserve IDs/slugs and keep natural features separate from launches. Resolve the lower Big Piney corridor before editing its coordinates.
  2. Repair shared classification behavior: Grubb Hollow serialization, the showers converter, off-channel landmark visibility and NPS override preservation. This prevents corrections from changing with platform, cache or sync.
  3. Apply verified record corrections: the four reviewed POI types, Rocky Falls association, Devils Well access context, Cowskin eligibility and the proven public/private corrections. Verify current conditions where an endpoint is newly enabled.
  4. Work the verification queue: Mammoth, ambiguous bridges/banks, duplicate candidates, same_place arrival links, remote pins and mileage pairs. Preserve documented exceptions.
  5. Recheck the complete flow: fresh lists, access details, old-client default response, offline bundle, campground cards, search, saved-plan links and a refreshed iOS device. Allow caches to refresh before judging production parity.
Prepared for Eddy • October 28, 2026 • Findings are point-in-time evidence and proposed changes. No production write was performed. All links to source code are pinned to the reviewed commit. External facts are attributed within the relevant finding.
